newsitem.title: GERMANY: IMF sees 1997 global growth of 4.4 pct - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: IMF sees 1997 global growth of 4.4 pct - newspaper.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund will forecast global economic growth of 4.4 percent for 1997, with the United States economy growing three percent and Japan by 2.2 percent, a German newspaper reported in Monday.
The Handelsblatt business daily said the IMF's World Economic Outlook, due for release later this week, predicted growth of 2.2 percent and 2.3 percent for German and France respectively.
World trade would grow by about seven percent this year and in 1998, the newspaper quoted the IMF as saying.
Foreign exchange rates were currently secured by fundamental data, it added.

The newspaper gave the IMF forecast for developing countries' growth as 6.6 percent this year. Asian developing countries would show the strongest growth at 8.3 percent, with Africa expanding 4.7 percent and Latin America by 4.4 percent.
Inflation among developing countries would ease to 9.7 percent from 13.1 percent in 1996.

Among the G7 industrialised nations, Japan would show the lowest inflation with 1.3 percent this year, Handelsblatt quoted the IMF report as showing. It predicted inflation rates of 1.6 percent for France, 1.8 percent for Germany and 2.9 percent for the United States.
